## These two sessions

| Session | When | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Lecture 1: Tidy data | Monday, Nov 2, 1:00–3:00 PM | ECC 100 LT |
| Lecture 2: Modelling lab | Wednesday, Nov 4, 1:00–3:00 PM | DHCC 4223 |

- Today we'll go over tidy data,
  how to wrangle and visualize it,
  and fit a first model
- I'll be live coding,
  so follow along or just watch
- On Wednesday we'll have a hands-on lab with medical data,
  where you'll clean data
  and fit linear and logistic regression models

## How these pages work

- Each section of the course website has the slides at the top
  and their contents written out below,
  so you can scroll and copy code without clicking through slides
- Course website:
  <https://chendaniely.github.io/MEDI-504A-2026W1-biostats/>

## Get your Codespace running

Start your Codespace now,
since the first start takes about 4 minutes.

1. Go to the [Codespaces](/setup-codespaces.qmd) page
   and click **Open in GitHub Codespaces**
2. When VS Code opens, trust the folder
3. Open `example.qmd` and render it

Today we're only testing the Codespace.
On Wednesday you'll fork the repository
and work in your own copy.

## Where we are

![](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/diagrams/data-science/base.png){fig-alt="The data science workflow: import, tidy, then a cycle of transform, visualize and model, then communicate." width="80%"}

This is the data science workflow from *R for Data Science*.
Today we'll mostly be in the "tidy" and "transform" steps,
and get a first look at "visualize" and "model".

Diagram from *R for Data Science* (2e),
